content: For individuals with blood pressure equal to or greater than 130/80 mmHg, the treatment strategy involves a combination of lifestyle modifications and pharmacologic interventions to lower blood pressure to below 130/80 mmHg. Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are the preferred pharmacologic agents for patients with both diabetes and hypertension, as these medications offer significant cardiovascular protective effects. Achieving the target blood pressure often necessitates the use of multiple medications. The selection of these drugs should prioritize minimizing adverse effects while also reducing cardiovascular risks. Combination therapy may involve the use of ACE inhibitors or ARBs alongside diuretics or calcium channel blockers to optimize blood pressure control.
